Hi Claire — thanks for looping KPMG. A few technical clarifications to help your DPIA: 

1) Data categories: Redwood processes user-provided prompts, assistant outputs, metadata (timestamps, request IDs), and optional customer-provided customer data when configured. We do not train models on customer prompt content in hosted mode; that is contractually controlled in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors & transfers: the attached CSV is the canonical inventory as of 2026-10-25. For transfers outside the EEA we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) plus additional technical controls (encryption in transit, customer-managed KMS for Private deployments). If Medica needs a data residency guarantee for EU-only processing, our Private offering (VPC/air-gapped) is available and we can scope that separately.

3) Audit evidence & frequency: For typical hosted customers we provide:
   - SOC2 Type II report (summary and redacted attachments) on request (NDA required).
   - Extracts of access logs, configuration snapshots, and redacted key rotation records for a given date range.
   - For high-sensitivity customers we offer periodic remote evidence collection (every 6 months) and a paid on-site option.

4) DPIA input sheet: I've started populating the DPIA-Inputs-Medica.xlsx with the processing descriptions, lawful bases, data minimization notes, and residual risk rows. Please see the draft tab and comment directly; I'll update based on KPMG feedback.
